title: ACGME Common Program Requirements (Fellowship)
description: The Common Program Requirements (Fellowship) define what every ACGME-accredited fellowship program must do. Fellowship is advanced GME beyond a core residency program; the CPR (Fellowship) parallels the Residency CPR with key distinctions reflecting that fellows have already completed residency.

browseContent.text: The Fellowship CPR governs ACGME-accredited fellowship (subspecialty) programs. Structurally, it parallels the Residency CPR, but key distinctions reflect that fellows enter having already completed a core residency and are able to practice autonomously in their core specialty.
Major differences from the Residency CPR

items: Program Director must possess subspecialty expertise; no explicit three-year experience requirement
Program Director must hold current certification in the subspecialty (not the core specialty)
Two options exist for fellow eligibility (Option 1 includes RCPSC/CFPC/ACGME-I Advanced; Option 2 limits to ACGME/AOA)
Fellow Eligibility Exception (Section 3.2.b) permits an exceptionally qualified international graduate under specific conditions
Subspecialty-specific Milestones (not specialty Milestones) used for evaluation
Section 4.12 requires pain management instruction where applicable to the subspecialty
Section 6.9.c: Fellows should serve in a supervisory role to junior fellows AND residents (Detail)
Programs must ensure fellow education does not compromise core residents' education
Faculty Survey: Section 2.10.a requires faculty members to complete the annual ACGME Faculty Survey
PGY-1 supervision requirement does not directly apply (fellows are post-residency)

browseContent.text: Section 1 (Oversight), Section 2 (Personnel — apart from PD qualifications and the Faculty Survey requirement), Section 5 (Evaluation framework, CCC, Annual Program Evaluation, board certification reporting using a 7-year cohort), and Section 6 (Learning and Working Environment, supervision levels, well-being, work hours: 80/week averaged over 4 weeks; 14 hours after 24-hour call; 1 day off in 7; up to 88 hours by exception; moonlighting counts toward 80) carry over essentially unchanged from the Residency CPR with "fellow" substituted for "resident".

flashcards.front: How is "Fellowship" defined in the introduction to the Fellowship CPR?
flashcards.back: Fellowship is advanced graduate medical education beyond a core residency program for physicians who desire to enter more specialized practice. Fellows have completed residency and are able to practice autonomously in their core specialty.

citation.source: CPR Fellowship, Introduction — Definition of Graduate Medical Education
citation.quote: Fellowship is advanced graduate medical education beyond a core residency program for physicians who desire to enter more specialized practice… Fellows who have completed residency are able to practice autonomously in their core specialty. The prior medical experience and expertise of fellows distinguish them from physicians entering residency.

flashcards.front: What are the qualifications required of a fellowship Program Director?
flashcards.back: The program director must possess subspecialty expertise and qualifications acceptable to the Review Committee. (Notably, unlike the Residency CPR, there is no explicit three-year educational/administrative experience requirement in the Fellowship CPR.)

citation.quote: 2.4. Qualifications of the Program Director: The program director must possess subspecialty expertise and qualifications acceptable to the Review Committee. (Core)

flashcards.front: What board certification must a fellowship Program Director hold?
flashcards.back: Current certification in the subspecialty by the American Board of [subspecialty] or by the American Osteopathic Board of [subspecialty], or subspecialty qualifications acceptable to the Review Committee.

citation.quote: 2.4.a. The program director must possess current certification in the subspecialty for which they are the program director by the American Board of _____ or by the American Osteopathic Board of _____, or subspecialty qualifications that are acceptable to the Review Committee. (Core)

flashcards.front: What certification must subspecialty physician faculty members hold?
flashcards.back: Current certification in the subspecialty by the American Board of [subspecialty] or the American Osteopathic Board of [subspecialty], or qualifications acceptable to the Review Committee.

citation.quote: 2.9. Subspecialty Physician Faculty Members. Subspecialty physician faculty members must have current certification in the subspecialty by the American Board of _____ or the American Osteopathic Board of _____, or possess qualifications judged acceptable to the Review Committee. (Core)

flashcards.front: What is required of "any other specialty physician faculty members" who are not subspecialty-certified?
flashcards.back: They must have current certification in their specialty by the appropriate ABMS member board or AOA certifying board, or possess qualifications judged acceptable to the Review Committee.

citation.quote: 2.9.a. Any other specialty physician faculty members must have current certification in their specialty by the appropriate American Board of Medical Specialties (ABMS) member board or American Osteopathic Association (AOA) certifying board, or possess qualifications judged acceptable to the Review Committee. (Core)

flashcards.front: What is the annual survey requirement for fellowship faculty?
flashcards.back: Faculty members must complete the annual ACGME Faculty Survey.

citation.quote: 2.10.a. Faculty members must complete the annual ACGME Faculty Survey.

flashcards.front: How are core faculty members defined in the Fellowship CPR?
flashcards.back: Core faculty members must have a significant role in the education and supervision of fellows, must devote a significant portion of their entire effort to fellow education and/or administration, and must — as a component of their activities — teach, evaluate, and provide formative feedback to fellows.

citation.quote: Core faculty members must have a significant role in the education and supervision of fellows and must devote a significant portion of their entire effort to fellow education and/or administration, and must, as a component of their activities, teach, evaluate, and provide formative feedback to fellows. (Core)

flashcards.front: What are the two options for fellow eligibility regarding required clinical education?
flashcards.back: Option 1: All required clinical education must be completed in an ACGME-accredited residency, AOA-approved residency, a program with ACGME-I Advanced Specialty Accreditation, or an RCPSC- or CFPC-accredited residency in Canada. Option 2 (more restrictive): only ACGME-accredited or AOA-approved residency programs. The Review Committee selects which option applies to its subspecialty.

citation.quote: 3.2. Eligibility Requirements – Fellowship Programs [Review Committee to choose one of the following:] Option 1: All required clinical education for entry into ACGME-accredited fellowship programs must be completed in an ACGME-accredited residency program, an AOA-approved residency program, a program with ACGME International (ACGME-I) Advanced Specialty Accreditation, or a Royal College of Physicians and Surgeons of Canada (RCPSC)-accredited or College of Family Physicians of Canada (CFPC)-accredited residency program located in Canada. (Core) Option 2: All required clinical education for entry into ACGME-accredited fellowship programs must be completed in an ACGME-accredited residency program or an AOA-approved residency program. (Core)

flashcards.front: What Milestones evaluations must fellowship programs receive for entering fellows?
flashcards.back: Programs must receive verification of each entering fellow's level of competence in the required field using Milestones evaluations from the core residency program — ACGME, ACGME-I, or CanMEDS Milestones if Option 1, or ACGME Milestones if Option 2. The ADS "Residency Milestone Retrieval" feature provides access to these reports.

citation.quote: 3.2.a. [If Review Committee selected Option 1 above:] Fellowship programs must receive verification of each entering fellow's level of competence in the required field using ACGME, ACGME-I, or CanMEDS Milestones evaluations from the core residency program. (Core) [If Review Committee selected Option 2 above:] Fellowship programs must receive verification of each entering fellow's level of competence in the required field using ACGME Milestones evaluations from the core residency program. (Core)

flashcards.front: What is the Fellow Eligibility Exception?
flashcards.back: An ACGME-accredited fellowship program may accept an exceptionally qualified international graduate applicant who does not satisfy the standard eligibility requirements if ALL of these are met: (a) evaluation by the program director and fellowship selection committee of the applicant's suitability based on prior training and summative evaluations; (b) review and approval of the applicant's exceptional qualifications by the GMEC; (c) verification of ECFMG certification. Applicants accepted through this exception must be evaluated by the CCC within 12 weeks of matriculation.

citation.quote: 3.2.b.1. An ACGME-accredited fellowship program may accept an exceptionally qualified international graduate applicant who does not satisfy the eligibility requirements listed in 3.2, but who does meet all of the following additional qualifications and conditions: (Core) 3.2.b.1.a. evaluation by the program director and fellowship selection committee of the applicant's suitability to enter the program, based on prior training and review of the summative evaluations of training in the core specialty; and, (Core) 3.2.b.1.b. review and approval of the applicant's exceptional qualifications by the GMEC; and, (Core) 3.2.b.1.c. verification of Educational Commission for Foreign Medical Graduates (ECFMG) certification. (Core) 3.2.b.2. Applicants accepted through this exception must have an evaluation of their performance by the Clinical Competency Committee within 12 weeks of matriculation. (Core)

flashcards.front: What does the Background and Intent state about applicants accepted under the Fellow Eligibility Exception regarding board certification?
flashcards.back: Applicants being considered for these positions must be informed that their training may not lead to certification by ABMS member boards or AOA certifying boards.

citation.source: CPR Fellowship, Section 3.2.b — Background and Intent
citation.quote: Applicants being considered for these positions must be informed of the fact that their training may not lead to certification by ABMS member boards or AOA certifying boards.

flashcards.front: Within how many weeks must the Clinical Competency Committee evaluate a fellow accepted through the Fellow Eligibility Exception?
flashcards.back: Within 12 weeks of matriculation.

citation.quote: 3.2.b.2. Applicants accepted through this exception must have an evaluation of their performance by the Clinical Competency Committee within 12 weeks of matriculation. (Core)

flashcards.front: What governs Fellow Complement?
flashcards.back: The program director must not appoint more fellows than approved by the Review Committee. Programs must request approval for all complement changes (temporary or permanent) through ADS; permanent increases require prior Review Committee approval.

citation.quote: 3.3. Fellow Complement. The program director must not appoint more fellows than approved by the Review Committee. (Core) Background and Intent: Programs are required to request approval of all complement changes, whether temporary or permanent, by the Review Committee through ADS. Permanent increases require prior approval from the Review Committee and temporary increases may also require approval.

flashcards.front: What is required for a Fellow Transfer?
flashcards.back: The program must obtain verification of previous educational experiences and a summative competency-based performance evaluation prior to acceptance of a transferring fellow, and Milestones evaluations upon matriculation.

citation.quote: 3.4. Fellow Transfers. The program must obtain verification of previous educational experiences and a summative competency-based performance evaluation prior to acceptance of a transferring fellow, and Milestones evaluations upon matriculation. (Core)

flashcards.front: What pain management requirement is specific to fellowship programs?
flashcards.back: The program must provide instruction and experience in pain management if applicable for the subspecialty, including recognition of the signs of substance use disorder.

citation.quote: 4.12. Curriculum Organization and Fellow Experiences – Pain Management. The program must provide instruction and experience in pain management if applicable for the subspecialty, including recognition of the signs of substance use disorder. (Core)

flashcards.front: What Milestones are used for a fellow's final evaluation?
flashcards.back: The subspecialty-specific Milestones (and when applicable the subspecialty-specific Case Logs) must be used to ensure fellows are able to engage in autonomous practice upon completion of the program.

citation.quote: 5.2.a. The subspecialty-specific Milestones, and when applicable the subspecialty-specific Case Logs, must be used as tools to ensure fellows are able to engage in autonomous practice upon completion of the program. (Core)

flashcards.front: What is the minimum composition of a Fellowship Clinical Competency Committee?
flashcards.back: At a minimum, three members, at least one of whom is a core faculty member. Members must be faculty members from the same program or other programs, or other health professionals who have extensive contact and experience with the program's fellows.

citation.quote: 5.3.a. At a minimum the Clinical Competency Committee must include three members, at least one of whom is a core faculty member. Members must be faculty members from the same program or other programs, or other health professionals who have extensive contact and experience with the program's fellows. (Core)

flashcards.front: How often must the fellowship Clinical Competency Committee review fellow evaluations?
flashcards.back: At least semi-annually (every 6 months).

citation.quote: 5.3.b. The Clinical Competency Committee must review all fellow evaluations at least semi-annually. (Core)

flashcards.front: What Milestones does the fellowship CCC determine progress on?
flashcards.back: The subspecialty-specific Milestones.

citation.quote: 5.3.c. The Clinical Competency Committee must determine each fellow's progress on achievement of the subspecialty-specific Milestones. (Core)

flashcards.front: What is the supervisory role of senior fellows in the Fellowship CPR?
flashcards.back: Fellows should serve in a supervisory role to junior fellows AND residents in recognition of their progress toward independence, based on the needs of each patient and the skills of the individual resident or fellow. This is classified as a Detail requirement.

citation.quote: 6.9.c. Fellows should serve in a supervisory role to junior fellows and residents in recognition of their progress toward independence, based on the needs of each patient and the skills of the individual resident or fellow. (Detail)

flashcards.front: How is "conditional independence" defined in the Fellowship CPR?
flashcards.back: Graded, progressive responsibility for patient care with defined oversight. (Identical definition to the Residency CPR.)

citation.source: CPR Fellowship, Section 6.10.a — Background and Intent
citation.quote: Background and Intent: The ACGME Glossary of Terms defines conditional independence as: Graded, progressive responsibility for patient care with defined oversight.

flashcards.front: What is the additional concern noted regarding "other learners" in the Fellowship CPR (compared to Residency)?
flashcards.back: In addition to ensuring that the presence of other learners doesn't negatively impact fellows' education, the Fellowship CPR also notes that fellows' education must not compromise core residents' education.

citation.source: CPR Fellowship, Section 1.11 — Background and Intent
citation.quote: 1.11. Other Learners and Health Care Personnel. The presence of other learners and other health care personnel, including but not limited to residents from other programs, subspecialty fellows, and advanced practice providers, must not negatively impact the appointed fellows' education. (Core) Background and Intent: …Programs have a responsibility to monitor the learning environment to ensure that fellows' education is not compromised by the presence of other providers and learners, and that fellows' education does not compromise core residents' education.

flashcards.front: What is the maximum weekly work hour limit for fellows?
flashcards.back: 80 hours per week, averaged over a four-week period, inclusive of all in-house clinical and educational activities, clinical work done from home, and all moonlighting. (Same as residency.)

citation.quote: Clinical and educational work hours must be limited to no more than 80 hours per week, averaged over a four-week period, inclusive of all in-house clinical and educational activities, clinical work done from home, and all moonlighting. (Core)

flashcards.front: How many hours must fellows have free of clinical work after 24 hours of in-house call?
flashcards.back: At least 14 hours.

citation.quote: 6.21.a. Fellows must have at least 14 hours free of clinical work and education after 24 hours of in-house call. (Core)

flashcards.front: Does the Fellowship CPR prohibit PGY-1-level moonlighting (as the Residency CPR does)?
flashcards.back: No. The Fellowship CPR Section 6.25.a requires that moonlighting time count toward the 80-hour weekly maximum, but does not include the PGY-1 prohibition (since fellows are post-residency). Moonlighting must not interfere with educational goals or patient safety.

citation.quote: 6.25. Moonlighting. Moonlighting must not interfere with the ability of the fellow to achieve the goals and objectives of the educational program, and must not interfere with the fellow's fitness for work nor compromise patient safety. (Core) 6.25.a. Time spent by fellows in internal and external moonlighting (as defined in the ACGME Glossary of Terms) must be counted toward the 80-hour maximum weekly limit. (Core)

flashcards.front: Which cohort of fellowship graduates must programs report board certification status for, annually in ADS?
flashcards.back: The cohort of board-eligible fellows that graduated seven years earlier.

citation.quote: 5.6.e. Programs must report, in ADS, board certification status annually for the cohort of board-eligible fellows that graduated seven years earlier. (Core)

flashcards.front: How does the 80% pass rate "safe harbor" work for board certification compliance?
flashcards.back: For each of the exams referenced in Sections 5.6 – 5.6.c, any program whose graduates over the specified time period have achieved an 80 percent pass rate will have met the requirement, regardless of the program's percentile rank in that subspecialty.

citation.quote: 5.6.d. For each of the exams referenced in 5.6. – 5.6.c., any program whose graduates over the time period specified in the requirement have achieved an 80 percent pass rate will have met this requirement, no matter the percentile rank of the program for pass rate in that subspecialty. (Outcome)

flashcards.front: What is the pass-rate threshold for board certification (annual written exam)?
flashcards.back: For subspecialties with an annual written exam, in the preceding three years, the program's aggregate pass rate for first-time test-takers must be higher than the bottom fifth percentile of programs in that subspecialty.

citation.quote: 5.6. Board Certification. For subspecialties in which the ABMS member board and/or AOA certifying board offer(s) an annual written exam, in the preceding three years, the program's aggregate pass rate of those taking the examination for the first time must be higher than the bottom fifth percentile of programs in that subspecialty. (Outcome)

flashcards.front: What must the fellowship Program Evaluation Committee distribute, and to whom?
flashcards.back: The Annual Program Evaluation, including the action plan, must be distributed to and discussed with the fellows and the members of the teaching faculty, and be submitted to the DIO.

citation.quote: 5.5.g. The Annual Program Evaluation, including the action plan, must be distributed to and discussed with the fellows and the members of the teaching faculty, and be submitted to the DIO. (Core)

flashcards.front: What Self-Study requirement applies to fellowship programs?
flashcards.back: The program must participate in a Self-Study and submit it to the DIO.

citation.quote: 5.5.h. The program must participate in a Self-Study and submit it to the DIO. (Core)

mcQuestions.stem: Which of the following best describes the experience requirement for a fellowship Program Director, per the Fellowship CPR?
options: At least 3 years of educational/administrative experience, mirroring the Residency CPR
Subspecialty expertise and qualifications acceptable to the Review Committee; no explicit minimum-years-of-experience requirement
5 years of subspecialty practice required
Completion of a fellowship in the subspecialty within the past 10 years
mcQuestions.explanation: The Fellowship CPR (Section 2.4) requires only that the PD possess subspecialty expertise and qualifications acceptable to the Review Committee. The explicit three-year educational/administrative experience requirement found in the Residency CPR does NOT appear in the Fellowship CPR.

citation.quote: 2.4. Qualifications of the Program Director: The program director must possess subspecialty expertise and qualifications acceptable to the Review Committee. (Core)

mcQuestions.stem: A fellowship Program Director must hold current certification in:
options: The core specialty only
The subspecialty for which they are the program director, OR equivalent qualifications acceptable to the Review Committee
Either the core specialty or the subspecialty — programs may choose
Any specialty within internal medicine or surgery
mcQuestions.explanation: Section 2.4.a requires current certification in the subspecialty for which they are the program director, by the appropriate American Board or American Osteopathic Board, or subspecialty qualifications acceptable to the Review Committee.

citation.quote: 2.4.a. The program director must possess current certification in the subspecialty for which they are the program director by the American Board of _____ or by the American Osteopathic Board of _____, or subspecialty qualifications that are acceptable to the Review Committee. (Core)

mcQuestions.stem: Per Section 2.10.a of the Fellowship CPR, what annual survey requirement applies to fellowship faculty?
options: Faculty must complete an annual program evaluation survey distributed by the GMEC
Faculty members must complete the annual ACGME Faculty Survey
Faculty must complete an annual fellow satisfaction survey
There is no annual survey requirement for fellowship faculty
mcQuestions.explanation: Section 2.10.a explicitly requires that faculty members complete the annual ACGME Faculty Survey. This requirement is unique to the Fellowship CPR; the Residency CPR does not contain an identical numbered requirement.

citation.quote: 2.10.a. Faculty members must complete the annual ACGME Faculty Survey.

mcQuestions.stem: A subspecialty's Review Committee has selected "Option 1" for fellow eligibility. Which of the following residency programs would qualify a candidate?
options: Only ACGME-accredited and AOA-approved residency programs
ACGME-accredited, AOA-approved, ACGME-I Advanced Specialty Accreditation programs, OR RCPSC- or CFPC-accredited residencies in Canada
Any internationally recognized residency program
Only programs in the United States
mcQuestions.explanation: Option 1 (Section 3.2) includes: ACGME-accredited residency, AOA-approved residency, ACGME-I Advanced Specialty Accreditation program, OR an RCPSC- or CFPC-accredited residency in Canada. Option 2 is more restrictive and would limit to only ACGME-accredited or AOA-approved residencies.

citation.quote: Option 1: All required clinical education for entry into ACGME-accredited fellowship programs must be completed in an ACGME-accredited residency program, an AOA-approved residency program, a program with ACGME International (ACGME-I) Advanced Specialty Accreditation, or a Royal College of Physicians and Surgeons of Canada (RCPSC)-accredited or College of Family Physicians of Canada (CFPC)-accredited residency program located in Canada. (Core)

mcQuestions.stem: A fellowship program is considering accepting an exceptionally qualified international graduate under the Fellow Eligibility Exception (Section 3.2.b). Which of the following is REQUIRED?
options: Approval by the Sponsoring Institution's CEO
Review and approval of the applicant's exceptional qualifications by the GMEC AND verification of ECFMG certification
Successful completion of USMLE Step 3
Recommendation by an ABMS board member
mcQuestions.explanation: Section 3.2.b.1 requires three specific conditions for acceptance under the exception, all of which must be met: (a) evaluation by the PD and selection committee of the applicant's suitability; (b) review and approval by the GMEC; (c) verification of ECFMG certification. Section 3.2.b.2 additionally requires CCC evaluation within 12 weeks of matriculation.

citation.quote: 3.2.b.1.b. review and approval of the applicant's exceptional qualifications by the GMEC; and, (Core) 3.2.b.1.c. verification of Educational Commission for Foreign Medical Graduates (ECFMG) certification. (Core)

mcQuestions.stem: Within how many weeks of matriculation must the Clinical Competency Committee evaluate a fellow accepted through the Fellow Eligibility Exception?
options: Within 4 weeks
Within 8 weeks
Within 12 weeks
Within 24 weeks
mcQuestions.explanation: Section 3.2.b.2 requires that applicants accepted through the Fellow Eligibility Exception have a CCC evaluation of their performance within 12 weeks of matriculation. This early evaluation ensures the program can quickly identify any concerns about the fellow's clinical competence.

citation.quote: 3.2.b.2. Applicants accepted through this exception must have an evaluation of their performance by the Clinical Competency Committee within 12 weeks of matriculation. (Core)

mcQuestions.stem: A program director is considering an exceptionally qualified IMG candidate under the Fellow Eligibility Exception. What must this applicant be informed of?
options: That they may not enter direct patient care for 6 months
That their training may not lead to certification by ABMS member boards or AOA certifying boards
That their salary will be reduced
That they will be assigned a mandatory mentor
mcQuestions.explanation: The Background and Intent for Section 3.2.b explicitly states that applicants being considered for these positions must be informed that their training may not lead to certification by ABMS member boards or AOA certifying boards.

citation.source: CPR Fellowship, Section 3.2.b — Background and Intent
citation.quote: Applicants being considered for these positions must be informed of the fact that their training may not lead to certification by ABMS member boards or AOA certifying boards.

mcQuestions.stem: Per Section 3.4 of the Fellowship CPR, what must a program obtain BEFORE accepting a transferring fellow?
options: Letters of recommendation from three faculty
Verification of previous educational experiences and a summative competency-based performance evaluation
The fellow's complete academic transcript from medical school
Approval by the ACGME
mcQuestions.explanation: Section 3.4 requires verification of previous educational experiences AND a summative competency-based performance evaluation prior to acceptance of a transferring fellow. Milestones evaluations are then required upon matriculation.

citation.quote: 3.4. Fellow Transfers. The program must obtain verification of previous educational experiences and a summative competency-based performance evaluation prior to acceptance of a transferring fellow, and Milestones evaluations upon matriculation. (Core)

mcQuestions.stem: Per the Fellowship CPR (Section 4.12), what must a fellowship program provide regarding pain management?
options: Nothing specific — this is covered in the Residency CPR only
Instruction and experience in pain management if applicable for the subspecialty, including recognition of the signs of substance use disorder
Annual pain management certification for all faculty
Mandatory rotation in a pain clinic
mcQuestions.explanation: Section 4.12 requires programs to provide instruction and experience in pain management if applicable for the subspecialty, including recognition of the signs of substance use disorder. (Core)

citation.quote: 4.12. Curriculum Organization and Fellow Experiences – Pain Management. The program must provide instruction and experience in pain management if applicable for the subspecialty, including recognition of the signs of substance use disorder. (Core)

mcQuestions.stem: What Milestones must the fellowship Clinical Competency Committee track each fellow's progress on?
options: Specialty-specific Milestones from the core residency
ACGME-I Foundational Milestones
Subspecialty-specific Milestones
USMLE Step 3 score progression
mcQuestions.explanation: Section 5.3.c requires the CCC to determine each fellow's progress on achievement of the subspecialty-specific Milestones (distinct from the specialty-specific Milestones used in residency).

citation.quote: 5.3.c. The Clinical Competency Committee must determine each fellow's progress on achievement of the subspecialty-specific Milestones. (Core)

mcQuestions.stem: The Fellowship Clinical Competency Committee must include at minimum how many members, and what is required of one of them?
options: Two members, with both being core faculty
Three members, at least one of whom is a core faculty member
Five members, all from the same subspecialty
Four members, with the program director as chair
mcQuestions.explanation: Section 5.3.a requires at minimum three members, at least one of whom is a core faculty member. Members must be faculty from the same or other programs, or other health professionals with extensive contact and experience with the program's fellows.

citation.quote: 5.3.a. At a minimum the Clinical Competency Committee must include three members, at least one of whom is a core faculty member. Members must be faculty members from the same program or other programs, or other health professionals who have extensive contact and experience with the program's fellows. (Core)

mcQuestions.stem: Per Section 6.9.c of the Fellowship CPR, what is the supervisory expectation for fellows regarding junior trainees?
options: Fellows must not supervise any trainees
Fellows should serve in a supervisory role to junior fellows only
Fellows should serve in a supervisory role to junior fellows AND residents, based on progress toward independence and skills
Fellows must take on full attending responsibility within their first year
mcQuestions.explanation: Section 6.9.c (Detail requirement) states fellows should serve in a supervisory role to junior fellows AND residents in recognition of their progress toward independence, based on the needs of each patient and the skills of the individual resident or fellow.

citation.quote: 6.9.c. Fellows should serve in a supervisory role to junior fellows and residents in recognition of their progress toward independence, based on the needs of each patient and the skills of the individual resident or fellow. (Detail)

mcQuestions.stem: Per the Background and Intent for Section 1.11 in the Fellowship CPR, what additional concern does the Fellowship CPR raise (compared to the Residency CPR) regarding other learners?
options: That advanced practice providers be excluded from teaching teams
That fellows' education must not compromise core residents' education
That medical students cannot rotate on fellow services
That subspecialty fellows must defer to senior fellows in all clinical decisions
mcQuestions.explanation: The Fellowship CPR adds the specific concern that fellows' education must not compromise core residents' education — a unique two-way consideration that recognizes fellows can themselves be the "other learners" who affect residents.

citation.source: CPR Fellowship, Section 1.11 — Background and Intent
citation.quote: Programs have a responsibility to monitor the learning environment to ensure that fellows' education is not compromised by the presence of other providers and learners, and that fellows' education does not compromise core residents' education.

mcQuestions.stem: Does the Fellowship CPR contain a prohibition on PGY-1 moonlighting, like the Residency CPR does?
options: Yes — first-year fellows may not moonlight
Yes — the language is identical
No — the PGY-1 moonlighting prohibition does not apply to fellowship; however, all fellow moonlighting must count toward the 80-hour weekly limit
Yes, but only for the first six months of the fellowship
mcQuestions.explanation: The Fellowship CPR Section 6.25 retains the requirement that moonlighting count toward the 80-hour weekly limit and must not interfere with educational goals or patient safety, but does NOT include a PGY-1-level prohibition (since fellows are post-residency).

citation.quote: 6.25.a. Time spent by fellows in internal and external moonlighting (as defined in the ACGME Glossary of Terms) must be counted toward the 80-hour maximum weekly limit. (Core)

mcQuestions.stem: For which cohort must fellowship programs annually report board certification status in ADS?
options: The most recent graduating cohort
The cohort that graduated 3 years earlier
The cohort of board-eligible fellows that graduated 7 years earlier
All graduates from the past 10 years cumulatively
mcQuestions.explanation: Section 5.6.e parallels the Residency CPR: programs must report in ADS, annually, the board certification status of the cohort of board-eligible fellows that graduated seven years earlier (graduates are eligible for up to seven years from fellowship graduation for initial certification).

citation.quote: 5.6.e. Programs must report, in ADS, board certification status annually for the cohort of board-eligible fellows that graduated seven years earlier. (Core)

mcQuestions.stem: A subspecialty's board offers an annual written exam. A program's first-time pass rate ranks in the bottom 3rd percentile for that subspecialty, but the program's overall first-time pass rate is 82% over the past three years. Per the Fellowship CPR, has this program met the board certification requirement?
options: No — because the program ranks below the fifth percentile
Yes — because the program's 82% pass rate exceeds the 80% threshold safe harbor
Only if the Review Committee grants a special exception
Only after a Self-Study is completed
mcQuestions.explanation: Section 5.6.d creates a safe harbor: any program achieving an 80% pass rate over the specified time period has met the requirement, REGARDLESS of percentile rank in that subspecialty. So an 82% rate satisfies the requirement even if the program ranks below the 5th percentile.

citation.quote: 5.6.d. For each of the exams referenced in 5.6. – 5.6.c., any program whose graduates over the time period specified in the requirement have achieved an 80 percent pass rate will have met this requirement, no matter the percentile rank of the program for pass rate in that subspecialty. (Outcome)

mcQuestions.stem: For a subspecialty with an annual written board examination, what is the pass-rate threshold (excluding the safe harbor)?
options: Above the bottom 10th percentile, over the preceding five years
Above the bottom 5th percentile of programs in that subspecialty, in the preceding three years
100% pass rate for all first-time test-takers
Above the median of all programs nationally
mcQuestions.explanation: Section 5.6 requires that, in the preceding three years, the program's aggregate first-time pass rate must be higher than the bottom fifth percentile of programs in that subspecialty (with the 80% safe harbor under 5.6.d as an alternative).

citation.quote: 5.6. Board Certification. For subspecialties in which the ABMS member board and/or AOA certifying board offer(s) an annual written exam, in the preceding three years, the program's aggregate pass rate of those taking the examination for the first time must be higher than the bottom fifth percentile of programs in that subspecialty. (Outcome)

mcQuestions.stem: What Milestones evaluations must a fellowship program receive when an entering fellow comes from a core residency program (Option 1 selected by Review Committee)?
options: Only ACGME Milestones
ACGME, ACGME-I, or CanMEDS Milestones evaluations from the core residency program
Only USMLE-based assessments
Internal board-administered Milestones
mcQuestions.explanation: Under Option 1, Section 3.2.a requires fellowship programs to receive verification of each entering fellow's level of competence using ACGME, ACGME-I, or CanMEDS Milestones evaluations from the core residency program. Under Option 2, only ACGME Milestones qualify.

citation.quote: 3.2.a. [If Review Committee selected Option 1 above:] Fellowship programs must receive verification of each entering fellow's level of competence in the required field using ACGME, ACGME-I, or CanMEDS Milestones evaluations from the core residency program. (Core)

mcQuestions.stem: How are the supervision levels defined for fellows in the Fellowship CPR?
options: Two levels: direct and indirect
Three levels: Direct Supervision (physically present), Indirect Supervision (immediately available), and Oversight (retrospective review with feedback after care)
Four levels including "remote"
Fellows do not require formal supervision classifications
mcQuestions.explanation: Section 6.7 of the Fellowship CPR uses the same three classifications as the Residency CPR: Direct Supervision (physically present during key portions of patient interaction), Indirect Supervision (not physically/concurrently present but immediately available), and Oversight (retrospective review with feedback after care is delivered).

citation.quote: 6.7. Direct Supervision. The supervising physician is physically present with the fellow during the key portions of the patient interaction… Indirect Supervision. The supervising physician is not providing physical or concurrent visual or audio supervision but is immediately available to the fellow for guidance and is available to provide appropriate direct supervision. Oversight. The supervising physician is available to provide review of procedures/encounters with feedback provided after care is delivered.

mcQuestions.stem: Where must the fellowship Annual Program Evaluation, including the action plan, be distributed and submitted?
options: Only to the program director and the Review Committee
Distributed to and discussed with fellows and teaching faculty, and submitted to the DIO
Submitted only to the Sponsoring Institution's CEO
Posted publicly on the program's website
mcQuestions.explanation: Section 5.5.g requires that the Annual Program Evaluation (including the action plan) be distributed to and discussed with fellows and members of the teaching faculty, and submitted to the DIO.

citation.quote: 5.5.g. The Annual Program Evaluation, including the action plan, must be distributed to and discussed with the fellows and the members of the teaching faculty, and be submitted to the DIO. (Core)

mcQuestions.stem: Per Section 5.5.h of the Fellowship CPR, what must each fellowship program participate in periodically?
options: A peer-program inspection
A Self-Study, which must be submitted to the DIO
Mandatory external accreditation by a third party
An ACGME-administered annual exam for all fellows
mcQuestions.explanation: Section 5.5.h requires the program to participate in a Self-Study and submit it to the DIO. This is part of the program's ongoing self-assessment cycle.

citation.quote: 5.5.h. The program must participate in a Self-Study and submit it to the DIO. (Core)

mcQuestions.stem: Which of the following is required regarding Fellow Complement?
options: The program director may appoint any number of fellows so long as the Sponsoring Institution agrees
The program director must not appoint more fellows than approved by the Review Committee; complement changes (temporary or permanent) require approval through ADS
Permanent increases can be made without ACGME involvement
Complement changes are at the discretion of the GMEC alone
mcQuestions.explanation: Section 3.3 requires that the program director not appoint more fellows than approved by the Review Committee. The Background and Intent clarifies that all complement changes — temporary or permanent — must be requested through ADS, with permanent increases requiring prior Review Committee approval.

citation.quote: 3.3. Fellow Complement. The program director must not appoint more fellows than approved by the Review Committee. (Core)

mcQuestions.stem: For a transferring fellow, which combination of items must the program obtain?
options: Letters of recommendation only
Verification of previous educational experiences AND a summative competency-based performance evaluation BEFORE acceptance, plus Milestones evaluations upon matriculation
Only the prior program's certificate of completion
Only ACGME accreditation status of the prior program
mcQuestions.explanation: Section 3.4 requires both verification of previous educational experiences AND a summative competency-based performance evaluation prior to acceptance of a transferring fellow, with Milestones evaluations required upon matriculation.

citation.quote: 3.4. Fellow Transfers. The program must obtain verification of previous educational experiences and a summative competency-based performance evaluation prior to acceptance of a transferring fellow, and Milestones evaluations upon matriculation. (Core)

mcQuestions.stem: How does the Fellowship CPR's definition of conditional independence differ from the Residency CPR's?
options: Fellows are granted automatic full independence
It is identical: Graded, progressive responsibility for patient care with defined oversight
It permits fellows to operate without any supervision after their first year
Conditional independence does not apply to fellows
mcQuestions.explanation: The definition is identical across both CPRs. The Fellowship CPR's Section 6.10.a Background and Intent references the ACGME Glossary of Terms: "Graded, progressive responsibility for patient care with defined oversight."

citation.source: CPR Fellowship, Section 6.10.a — Background and Intent
citation.quote: Background and Intent: The ACGME Glossary of Terms defines conditional independence as: Graded, progressive responsibility for patient care with defined oversight.

mcQuestions.stem: A fellowship program needs to verify subspecialty certification of physician faculty members. According to Section 2.9 of the Fellowship CPR, who must hold subspecialty certification?
options: Only the program director
Subspecialty physician faculty members, by the appropriate American Board or American Osteopathic Board, or possess qualifications judged acceptable to the Review Committee
All faculty members regardless of discipline
Only core faculty members
mcQuestions.explanation: Section 2.9 specifically addresses subspecialty physician faculty members, requiring current certification in the subspecialty (or qualifications acceptable to the Review Committee). Section 2.9.a separately addresses other-specialty physician faculty.

citation.quote: 2.9. Subspecialty Physician Faculty Members. Subspecialty physician faculty members must have current certification in the subspecialty by the American Board of _____ or the American Osteopathic Board of _____, or possess qualifications judged acceptable to the Review Committee. (Core)
